name: Volcanic & aviation ash
value: No red aviation codes found (24 Nov)
summary: No red aviation codes, VEI 4+ eruptions or ash-related airspace closures found by 24 Nov; Mayon at alert level 3
state: The Philippines raised Mayon's alert level on 30 Oct after an explosive eruption, and it stayed at level 3 with lava flows and ash plumes in early November (The Star; Nature World News, 4 Nov). The Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program lists continuing eruptions at volcanoes such as Semeru, Sangay and Fuego with routine ash advisories. No red aviation colour code near major air routes, VEI 4+ eruption or major ash-related airspace closure was found by 24 Nov, so Normal holds.
for_you: No volcanic ash is disrupting major air routes. Travellers to the Philippines or Indonesia may see local flight changes near active volcanoes; check with airlines and FCDO travel advice.
rubric_hit: Normal: no aviation colour code red and no large eruption found by 24 Nov

why: Major eruptions ground flights (Iceland 2010) and can cool the climate for years.
drivers: Volcanic unrest; impact depends on ash plume height and jet-stream direction.

rubric.alert: Major airspace closures from ash, or a VEI 4+ eruption.
rubric.watch: Aviation colour code orange/red at a volcano near major air routes, or a large eruption.
rubric.normal: No aviation colour code red; no large eruptions.
